newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen down amid Handlowy offer.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen down amid Handlowy offer.

text.p: Polish shares extended Tuesday's dip on Wednesday and analysts expected further falls under pressure from large Bank Handlowy privatisation offer and profit-taking after recent growth.
The main market's WIG index fell 1.1 percent, to 15,991.9, turnover fell 10 percent to 138.1 million zlotys ($43.2 million) on all three markets as 82 issues fell, 10 rose and 12 were flat.
The bourse rose 2.7 percent from last Wednesday to Monday.

"I expect falls even to intensify tomorrow and on Friday as it's the last chance for individual investors to subscribe in the first period for Handlowy...but the bourse should slow falls later," said Tomasz Cwintal, an analyst at BGZ brokerage.
Analysts said Tuesday's news of Standard & Poor's reaffirming its ratings for Poland should not influence the market despite some expectations of an upgrade.
"Investors will remain very positive on the country both in equity as well as debt issues," Daniel Schultz, analyst at Societe Generale in London told Reuters.

Analysts said in the longer-term the bourse should maintain its 2.5-month horizontal trend, perhaps with negative undertones, because of the undergoing and forthcoming large offers on the primary market.
They said Bank Handlowy public offer worth about one billion zlotys ($312 million) and expected June sale of copper giant KGHM were drawing capital from the bourse.

They also said many foreign investors stayed on the sidelines, because of forthcoming general election due in September and their absence and thinner trading volumes allowed domestic investors set the market's tone.

Construction and trading company Atlantis bourse debut was postponed until Thursday because realeased potentially market-sensitive data too late to allow all investors equal access to the information.
